theme: US air travel: BTS T-100 segment, DB1B fares, Form 41, on-time performance; repos that download and tidy them; TSA throughput scrapers
queries_run: gh search repos "airline on-time performance dataset" --sort updated
gh search repos "airport passenger traffic monthly"
gh search repos "airline capacity ASM RPM"
gh search repos "airfare data DB1B python" --sort updated

candidates.name: chengxdadp/tsa-passenger-volume
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily-updated pull of TSA daily checkpoint passenger-screening totals from tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes, complete annual series 2019-2025 plus YTD 2026 (through ~3 Sep 2026). Python scripts auto-refresh; ships time-series CSVs by year, YoY comparison charts, 7-day moving average, monthly seasonality.
candidates.why_useful: Duplicates the TSA throughput series we already hold, but this one is actively maintained through Sep 2026 (past our 2024 cutoff where our own TSA construction failed) and ships a ready one-command daily-pull script rather than a one-off snapshot — useful for a fresher nowcast attempt even though our prior TSA-since-2024 test failed on our own construction (gap 10).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold TSA throughput; this is a longer/fresher/actively-updated vintage with a reusable scraper

candidates.name: kw468/tsathroughput
candidates.what_it_holds: Hourly TSA checkpoint throughput totals from 2014 onward (per repo description "hourly tsa checkpoint totals, 2014-"); at least one visible file tsa_totals_2020_2021.csv. Hourly granularity is finer than the daily series we hold, and 2014 start is far older than typical TSA archive availability.
candidates.why_useful: If the hourly, 2014-onward file set is genuinely committed, this is materially finer-grained and longer than our existing daily TSA panel — worth a look even though our own TSA-since-2024 construction failed, since gap rules say catalogue longer/older/finer-grained versions regardless (gap 10).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We hold TSA throughput; this claims hourly granularity back to 2014, unverified beyond the visible 2020-2021 file
candidates.size_hint: unknown, likely multiple CSVs by year

candidates.name: mikelor/TsaThroughput-Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion data-lake repo (Apache-2.0, 9 commits) storing TSA Checkpoint Throughput files pulled and shaped by the paired mikelor/tsathroughput scraper/processing repo; has a /data folder. Exact date range and format not confirmed without a directory listing.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, licensed (Apache-2.0) TSA data mirror plus a paired open-source acquisition tool — lower confidence than kw468's repo on scope but the license is a plus for reuse.

candidates.name: onthebay98/tsa-forecast
candidates.what_it_holds: SARIMAX state-space probabilistic forecasting method for TSA checkpoint volumes; backtest window 2024-01-01 to 2026-02-22 (112+ weeks). NOTE: raw source code and data have been stripped from the public repo ("documentation only... actively deployed in production"); only ACF/forecast-error plot images remain in /data.
candidates.why_useful: Method-only reference (a public backtest window and SARIMAX framing for TSA nowcasting) but no runnable code or data — low value, flag mainly to avoid re-discovery.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Our own TSA-since-2024 nowcast attempt already failed; this is an independent method with no reusable artifact

candidates.name: VijayChamakuri/hub-delay-audit
candidates.what_it_holds: Auditing minimum-connection-time standards at 15 major US hub airports (focus on SFO, EWR, LGA, ORD, BOS, JFK, LAX, SEA, MSP, SLC) using two BTS datasets: On-Time Performance for Jan 2019 (583,985 flight records, 251MB) and the DB1B Coupon Survey 10% sample for Q1 2019 (9,846,816 itineraries, 1.9GB), joined at OperatingCarrier+DestinationAirport+Quarter across 5 carriers (AA, DL, UA, WN, AS, 91.5% of survey volume). Python, single quarter of data.
candidates.why_useful: This is the only repo found that actually demonstrates a working BTS T-100/On-Time + DB1B join pipeline end-to-end (download, clean, join, hub-level delay-buffer analysis) — a template for building a fresh, current-quarter T-100/DB1B pull for air-travel-demand cross-checks on ABNB nights (gap 10), even though the committed sample data is limited to Q1 2019.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: None; we hold no BTS T-100/DB1B pipeline
candidates.time_coverage: Q1 2019 only (Jan 2019 On-Time Performance, Q1 2019 DB1B)
candidates.size_hint: 251MB OTP + 1.9GB DB1B sample (per repo description; whether these large files are actually committed vs. downloaded by script is unconfirmed)

candidates.name: karansgotit/seattle-flight-reliability
candidates.what_it_holds: Historical reliability comparison tool for SEA-origin domestic flights built on BTS On-Time Performance data; MIT licensed, updated 12 Sep 2026 (most recently active BTS repo found).
candidates.why_useful: Recency and MIT license make it a plausible template for a fresh BTS On-Time pull script even though scope (Seattle-only reliability) is narrow and unrelated directly to nights/ADR; low direct fit to numbered gaps but real and current.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: None specific; generic BTS OTP analysis

candidates.name: zaynahjaved/bloomberg-flight-delays
candidates.what_it_holds: US flight delay prediction (48+ min arrival delay) using BTS On-Time Performance data and XGBoost.
candidates.why_useful: Generic ML-on-BTS-OTP project; catalogued only because BTS pull/clean code may be reusable for a T-100-style capacity/delay cross-check, but no unique data beyond the standard BTS download.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Generic BTS OTP re-use, no new data

candidates.name: lennyhuntley/csci-192-final-project
candidates.what_it_holds: Serverless AWS data-lakehouse pipeline ingesting the full BTS On-Time Performance dataset (carrier benchmarking, schedule padding, airspeed recovery metrics) as a course final project.
candidates.why_useful: Pipeline-only (S3/Lambda/Glue-style ELT for BTS OTP); potentially reusable as an ingestion template for a full historical BTS pull rather than month-by-month manual downloads, but no unique dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified, described as full BTS OTP history

notes: This theme is heavily saturated with one-off student/course projects re-running the same Kaggle-mirrored BTS On-Time Performance CSV with no new data or novel acquisition method; most were excluded per the cataloguing rules (generic ML boilerplate on a well-known dataset, no committed data of note). No repo surfaced containing a genuine T-100 SEGMENT (capacity/ASM/RPM by carrier-market) download tool, a DB1B FARE (not just coupon/itinerary count) dataset, or a Form 41 financial-schedule puller — those three specific BTS products (T-100 segment, DB1B market/fare tables, Form 41) appear essentially uncatalogued on GitHub under these search terms; worth a follow-up code-search pass (`gh search code "T_T100"` or similar) by a future scout given the 10/min code-search limit was reserved. TSA search terms surfaced a healthy cluster of scraper/mirror repos (tsa.gov passenger-volumes page is evidently easy to scrape) — chengxdadp's is the freshest (updated 7 Sep 2026) and closest to a genuine 'longer/fresher vintage' per the rules despite our own TSA-since-2024 construction having failed. VijayChamakuri/hub-delay-audit is the one repo that actually demonstrates joining BTS OTP with DB1B, useful as a working pipeline template even though its committed scope is a single 2019 quarter. No DB1B fare-market (not coupon) dataset, no OpenSky/ADS-B repos, and no Eurocontrol/airport-passenger-stats repos surfaced under these queries (searches for those terms returned zero results) — a broader query set (e.g. 'airport enplanements CSV', 'FAA TAF forecast download', 'flightera scraper') is likely needed by whichever scout covers airport/airline capacity more directly. gh search rate limits were not hit; all 6 gh calls succeeded on first try, well under budget.
